source.title: Irish Press, 5 June 1936, p. 7 ("Enniskillen urban area election")
source.publisher: Irish Press (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Votes as printed: 'Mr. J. McLoughlin (outgoing N.) securing 862 votes against 802 for Mr. G. Elliott (U.)'; 862-802=60, the majority printed elsewhere.

note: Triennial election of Fermanagh County Council. Polling day was Wednesday 3 June 1936 (results 'declared yesterday', Belfast News-Letter, 5 June 1936; the poll date is the statutory Wednesday and is provisional in the phase-A calendar). Two divisions were contested: Monea and Enniskillen urban. The Irish Press of 5 June 1936 prints both results with votes: Corrigan 548, Connor 376 at Monea, and McLoughlin 862, Elliott 802 at Enniskillen. The remaining eighteen divisions were uncontested and their members are named in the Northern Whig's nominations list of 30 April 1936. Structure and division names for the 1966-67 amalgamation are in notes/fermanagh-fcra-1969.md, from Fermanagh CRA, 'Fermanagh Facts' (1969). That is an advocacy pamphlet: use it for names only, not figures. Its register figures are disputed by Kingsley (2021) on the Omagh Rural District scheme. Read the page image before recording any number from it. The paper calls the division the 'urban area of Enniskillen'; it is Enniskillen Borough in the other rounds. The Belfast News-Letter's first-meeting report of 16 June 1936 confirms that Elliott was defeated and afterwards co-opted.
